body.p: Claims 1-10 were previously canceled. Claims 11-30 are currently pending. Claims 11, and 29 are currently amended.
Claims 11-16, 18-23, and 25-30 are rejected as being unpatentable over Chahine et al. (US 2017/0056644) in view of Chen et al. (US 2010/0041975).
1. Chen does not teach or suggest "repeat said generating the generated signal and said
sensing of the generated signal using the another textile-based ECG electrode pairing" as
recited by amended claims 11 and 29.
The present claims require "repeat said generating of the generated signal and said sensing of the generated signal using the another textile-based ECG electrode pairing."
The Office Action, at page 5, acknowledges that this limitation is not taught by Chahine. However, the Office Action cites Chen para. [0045] - [0046] as teaching this limitation.

Chen, paragraph 0045 describes the functionality of the system, which includes identifying electrodes and avoiding premature switching by allowing adequate time for circuitry stabilization. It also mentions that the system checks signal quality (i.e., at most every four seconds).
Chen, paragraphs 0046 describes considerations for signal quality, such as electrode-skin contact and electrode placement across the heart.
However, none of these paragraphs, nor the remainder of Chen, describe repeating said generating the generated signal and sensing of the generated signal as recited by the present claims.
By overlooking the generation of the generated signal by the controller device, the Office

Action improperly dissects the claim and focuses only on isolated elements, ignoring the role of the controller device, contrary to the principle that claims must be considered as a whole. As stated in MPEP § 2141.02: "In determining the differences between the prior art and the claims, the question under 35 U.S.C. 103 is not whether the differences themselves would have been obvious, but whether the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious."
At least for this reason, claims 11 and 29 are considered to be patentable over the cited art.
2. Chen does not teach or suggest "based on the sensing the generated signal generated by the
SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.3031.19 ... deselect the at least one determined textile-based ECG electrode from
ng, and select another textile-based ECG electrode pairing, repeat said
generate and said sense of the generated signal using the another textile-based ECG
electrode pairing" as recited by amended claims 11 and 29.
Claim 11 as amended requires certain steps in response to sensing the generated signal

generated by the controller device. In particular, deselecting the ECG electrode pairing, selecting another ECG electrode pairing, and repeating the process of generating and sensing the generated signal using the another electrode pairing. As discussed above, Chen does not have a generated signal generated by a controller device, and therefore, fails to teach the claimed ECG electrode pairing.
Instead, Chen describes "generate physiological data derived from the electrical signals." This is data coming from the patient, not from a controller device.
At least for this reason, claims 11 and 29 are considered to be patentable over the cited art.
